### Environment
- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- Official ChatGPT/Codex Linux desktop DEB package
- Desktop versions tested: 26.924.22138 and 26.901.41600
- Codex extension in VS Code on the same Ubuntu machine

### Issue
The standalone Linux desktop application displays the existing conversation list, but clicking a conversation does not load its contents.

The exact same conversations can be opened and continued successfully through:
- The Codex extension in VS Code on the same Ubuntu computer.
- The Remote feature in the ChatGPT iPhone app connected to this computer.

### Reproduction
1. Launch standalone ChatGPT/Codex Desktop on Ubuntu with the existing profile.
2. Click an existing conversation in the sidebar.
3. Its contents fail to load, although the conversation remains accessible in VS Code and iPhone Remote.

### Troubleshooting performed
- Downgraded desktop app; issue persisted.
- Tested with GPU acceleration disabled.
- Tested Wayland and X11 Ozone backends.
- Tested a fresh Electron profile: initially worked, but issue later returned.
- Tested resetting Session Storage and Local Storage separately, without success.
- SQLite `PRAGMA quick_check` returned `ok` for `thread_history_1.sqlite`, `state_5.sqlite`, `logs_2.sqlite` and `queue_1.sqlite`.
- App-server logs show desktop `thread/read` requests received, including request IDs prefixed `CodexWebviewProvider.webview:`. The available log extract does not establish whether the response completed or how the desktop processed it.
- DevTools shortcut Ctrl+Shift+I did not open DevTools.

### Expected behavior
Clicking an existing conversation opens its contents in the standalone desktop application, as in the VS Code extension.

### Actual behavior
Conversation list appears, but existing conversation contents fail to load in standalone desktop.

### Diagnostics and privacy
Sanitized logs/screenshots can be provided upon request. Full local session transcripts, databases and authentication files are intentionally not attached because they may contain private project data.

Related but not identical Linux Desktop report: #48354. An OpenAI support request has also been escalated.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.158.0 (installed via npm)  The managed app-server daemon is also running from the 0.158.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc release directory.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6-Sol

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200, build 26200, x64. Native Windows environment using PowerShell.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

The unwanted error windows are hosted by Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0.

### Codex doctor report

```json
Not collected yet.
```

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating Codex CLI to 0.158.0 on September 29, 2026, starting Codex or submitting a prompt causes dozens of terminal windows to appear almost immediately.

The windows display the following error:

```text
[error 2147942632 (0x800700e8) when launching `"git" -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=false rev-parse HEAD']
```

This happens repeatedly during normal use and makes the CLI very disruptive to use.

The approximate number of windows is based on visual observation; an exact count has not been captured.

I first noticed this behavior after the update. I have not yet performed a controlled comparison against the previously installed version, so I cannot confirm which release introduced it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed reproduction on my machine:

1. Use the npm-installed Codex CLI 0.158.0 in a native Windows PowerShell environment.
2. Start Codex. A managed app-server daemon from the 0.158.0 release is also running on this machine.
3. Observe dozens of terminal error windows appearing almost immediately.
4. Submit a prompt in Codex.
5. Observe another burst of terminal windows displaying the Git command and error shown above.

This is my current environment's reproduction, not yet a minimal isolated reproduction. I have not tested with the managed daemon disabled or with a clean configuration.

### What is the expected behavior?

Starting Codex and submitting prompts should not open additional visible terminal windows for background Git metadata queries.

Background commands such as `git rev-parse HEAD` should run without stealing focus or leaving terminal error windows behind. Any background launch failure should be handled internally and reported through diagnostics.

### Additional information

### Verified local observations

- Codex CLI npm package version: 0.158.0.
- Running managed app-server daemon executable: from the 0.158.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc release directory.
- Git for Windows version: 2.53.0.windows.2.
- Windows Terminal version: 1.24.11911.0.
- Git resolves to `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`.
- Windows error 232, corresponding to 0x800700E8, is reported locally as "The pipe is being closed."

### Independent Git check

The exact Git command shown in the error was executed directly in an existing local Git repository using .NET ProcessStartInfo with:

```text
UseShellExecute = false
CreateNoWindow = true
RedirectStandardOutput = true
RedirectStandardError = true
```

Command:

```text
git -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=false rev-parse HEAD
```

Result:

```text
Exit code: 0
Stdout: a valid HEAD commit hash
Stderr: empty
```

This confirms that the command succeeds in that repository when launched without creating a visible window. It does not reproduce Codex's launch path or establish the root cause.

### Related reports

Possibly related to:

- #48023 — primarily reports visible console windows when the managed daemon starts stdio MCP servers. Its discussion also includes background Git terminal windows at prompt submission.
- #44768 — reports visible console windows for hooks and shell commands executed by the shared app-server daemon.

I am reporting the Git-command error-window variant observed on 0.158.0. I have not confirmed whether it shares the same root cause as these reports. Please consolidate this issue if appropriate.

### Investigation status

The managed daemon's Windows child-process launch behavior is a possible area to investigate, including whether background Git processes are started with appropriate no-window creation flags.

I have not independently verified the relevant Codex source path or creation flags for this incident.

The following comparisons have not yet been performed:

- Running with the managed daemon disabled.
- Downgrading to the previously working version.
- Changing the default Windows terminal application.
- Reproducing with a clean configuration and no plugins, MCP servers, or command hooks.

Private repository names, paths, commit hashes, and raw session logs are omitted.

items.body:
### Environment

- Omarchy 4.0.4-1, Linux 7.2.5-3-omarchy, x86_64, Hyprland/Wayland.
- Affected Omarchy package: `openai-codex-desktop 26.924.22138-1`.
- Working after rollback: `openai-codex-desktop 26.915.31945-1`.

### Problem

New local Codex chats in multiple project folders remain indefinitely at **“Starting your task”**, even for a short greeting. Cloud tasks still work. In this reproduction, the bundled *local app-server actually received, ran, and completed the turn*, but the desktop renderer did not recognize its conversation ID and never displayed the response. This differs from reports in which `thread/start` / `turn/start` are never dispatched; whether the root cause is shared is unknown.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run ChatGPT/Codex Desktop 26.924.22138-1 on this Linux desktop.
2. Create a new local chat in a project folder, send a brief message (e.g., `hi`).
3. Observe “Starting your task” indefinitely. Repeat in another local folder: same result.
4. The app-server and renderer logs disagree about the outcome of the same conversation (see below).

**Expected:** The response appears and the chat becomes usable.

### Sanitized diagnostic evidence

On 2026-09-29, local time (UTC+03:00), for a **new** chat created after starting with a fresh desktop profile:

```text
10:35:55  app-server request: thread/start
10:35:55  app-server request: turn/start
10:35:55  renderer: [electron-message-handler] Received turn/started for unknown conversation
10:36:27  app-server event: turn/completed targeted_connections=1
10:36:27  renderer: [electron-message-handler] Received turn/completed for unknown conversation
```

Both renderer errors identified the same conversation as the task processed by the app-server. The message remained at “Starting your task” despite `turn/completed`. Conversation IDs, absolute project paths, and full logs are omitted for privacy.

### Troubleshooting / version comparison

- Fully quit and restart the desktop app: no change.
- Reinstalled **the same** 26.924.22138-1 package; `pacman -Qkk` reported 0 altered files: no change.
- Moved the Electron desktop profile (`~/.config/Codex`) to a backup and launched with a fresh profile, leaving `~/.codex` and projects untouched: **new local chats still failed** with the same `unknown conversation` errors.
- Tried different local project folders: same result.
- Fully quit, downgraded to the cached, signed `openai-codex-desktop-26.915.31945-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` using `sudo pacman -U`, and relaunched, **without restoring the previous profile**. A new local chat immediately displayed its reply. The 26.915 package passed `pacman -Qkk` (0 altered files).

**Temporary workaround:** On Omarchy, if the older signed package is still available locally: `sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/openai-codex-desktop-26.915.31945-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`. This is a downgrade, not a permanent fix; a normal package update may reinstall the affected version. Please ship a fixed Linux build.

Related Linux 26.924 reports: #48602, #48554. Omarchy package tracking: omacom/omarchy#13597. I am not asserting that the SIGCHLD issue discussed in #48554 is the cause of these specific `unknown conversation` events; that needs confirmation.

items.body:
# Windows sandbox refresh can time out while propagating a deny ACL and then treat an incomplete tree as complete

Consumer issue: Fredoooou/source-community#357

An unchanged full protected-root zero-model control using the qualified `v0.153.4-society.5` executable initialized successfully, then its first `society-model` command failed after 123,095 ms with:

`orchestrator_helper_timed_out: setup deadline exceeded during setup refresh helper`

No check command or model call ran. Guardian termination and native-admission release were positively confirmed.

A strict payload-free projection of the existing setup log identifies the exact boundary. Deny-read reconciliation planned 384 roots, completed roots 1-379 in about 175 ms, and stopped at root 380 after successful DACL read/build and before the `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` write returned. Root 380 maps to the qualified DeepSeek profile directory. Windows documents that this API propagates inheritable ACEs to existing descendants, so a large existing profile tree can keep this synchronous call inside the command's setup deadline.

There is also a retry-safety defect. The persistent state journals desired roots before ACL application. If propagation is interrupted after the parent ACE changes, a retry sees the matching parent ACE and skips the root, even though no durable fact proves propagation completed for all existing descendants.

Acceptance:

- Retain fail-closed exact-root protection; do not solve this by increasing deadlines or omitting retained protected roots.
- Emit opt-in/payload-free phase evidence: fixed phase, ordinal/count, operation boundary/result, and elapsed time only.
- Persist or otherwise establish a per-root propagation-completed fact tied to exact root identity and sandbox SID. Interrupted propagation must be safely resumable and must not be accepted solely from the parent ACE.
- Test interruption after parent write begins, retry, and denial of an existing descendant near the end of the tree.
- Test the unchanged completed-root fast path without rewriting or walking the tree.
- Preserve the current helper deadline, termination/reaping, singleflight, and no-path/no-payload logging constraints.

Evidence and source analysis are retained in `D:/SocietyLocalWork/2026-09-29/roadmap-recovery/provider-refresh-timeout-diagnosis.md`.

items.body:
### Summary

On my ChatGPT Pro 20x subscription (USD 200/month), the Codex web usage dashboard repeatedly shows **58% remaining immediately after a reload or opening a new page**, then automatically changes to **16% remaining** after the page has been left open. Reloading restores 58%, and the cycle repeats.

Captured responses from `GET /backend-api/wham/usage` show two different weekly usage values. The response reporting 42% used has a populated `account_id`; the response reporting 84% used has an empty `account_id`.

This is a correlation in the captured responses, not a confirmed root cause. I have not yet verified whether the requests differ in their account-selection headers.

### Environment

- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro 20x, USD 200/month
- Surface: Codex web usage dashboard, `https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/analytics#usage`
- Browser/device: Chrome 152 on a Chromebook
- UI language: Swedish (`sv-SE`)
- Observed: September 29, 2026, approximately 20:00–20:39 CEST (18:00–18:39 UTC)
- The behavior was observed before opening DevTools. Some later diagnostic screenshots were taken with mobile emulation enabled.

### Reproduction

1. Open or reload the usage dashboard.
2. Observe 58% weekly allowance remaining.
3. Leave the page open.
4. Observe the displayed allowance automatically change to 16%, without manually changing accounts or applying a reset.
5. Reload the page: 58% returns.
6. Inspect the usage requests in DevTools.

Earlier in the same observation period, the corresponding values were 59% and 18%.

### Captured API evidence

The following excerpts omit user identity, credentials, and unrelated fields. The populated account ID has been replaced with a placeholder.

**Response associated with 58% remaining:**

```json
{
  "account_id": "<redacted-nonempty-account-id>",
  "plan_type": "pro",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": true,
    "limit_reached": false,
    "primary_window": {
      "used_percent": 42,
      "limit_window_seconds": 604800,
      "reset_after_seconds": 339877,
      "reset_at": 1791046910
    },
    "secondary_window": null
  },
  "credits": {
    "balance": "18.7907035000"
  }
}
```

**Response associated with 16% remaining:**

```json
{
  "account_id": "",
  "plan_type": "pro",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": true,
    "limit_reached": false,
    "primary_window": {
      "used_percent": 84,
      "limit_window_seconds": 604800,
      "reset_after_seconds": 340035,
      "reset_at": 1791046910
    },
    "secondary_window": null
  },
  "credits": {
    "balance": "18.7907035000"
  }
}
```

Both responses identify the same user (identity omitted), report `plan_type: "pro"`, and have the same weekly window length, reset timestamp, and credit balance. The difference in `reset_after_seconds` reflects that the captures were taken at different times.

The reset time displayed in the UI remains October 3, 2026, 19:01 CEST.

### Expected behavior

Initial loading and subsequent automatic updates should use consistent account context and report a consistent weekly allowance for the subscription.

### Actual behavior and impact

The reported used percentage switches between 42% and 84%, producing 58% versus 16% remaining. The earlier UI pair of 59% versus 18% remaining also corresponds mathematically to 41% versus 82% used; API captures for that earlier pair are not included.

This makes it impossible to reliably plan work against the remaining allowance. I have **not** established which value governs actual usage enforcement, or that the subscription has been downgraded. Both captured responses still permit usage.

### Requested investigation

Please investigate:

- Why the usage responses alternate between a populated and empty `account_id`.
- Whether initial loading and background updates send or resolve different account context.
- Why the reported weekly used percentage differs by exactly a factor of two.
- Which allowance and account context actually govern usage enforcement for this Pro 20x subscription.

### Related reports

- #44251 — weekly quota oscillating between different states, documented in server response headers.
- #44245 — quota state changing and then reverting.

These reports have similar symptoms, but their reset timestamps also change. In my captures, the reset timestamp remains identical. I am not claiming a shared root cause.

Only sanitized response excerpts are included here; no authorization headers, cookies, or cURL exports are attached.

items.body:
## Summary
Unix-socket app-server startup regressed on unrooted Android/Termux after the protected socket-directory change. Codex CLI 0.154.0 works on the same device; 0.156.1 and current stable 0.159.1 exit immediately with `Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` when started with `app-server --listen unix://` or an explicit Unix socket path.

The failure occurs before any model request or sandboxed command. SSH authentication itself succeeds; Desktop subsequently reports `socket hang up` because its app-server proxy has no listening server.

## Version / environment
- Latest tested: `codex-cli 0.159.1` (official standalone `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` package; SHA-256 verified).
- Known working: 0.154.0. Also reproduced on 0.156.1.
- Android, native Termux, aarch64, Linux kernel 4.14.113, ordinary non-root Android app UID.
- `/tmp` does not exist. `/` is read-only; `mkdir /tmp` returns `Read-only file system`.
- Termux has a valid, writable `$TMPDIR` under its application prefix.
- Reproduces with an isolated Codex home and empty configuration, without authentication. Subscription/model therefore not applicable to the reproducer.
- Observed via Windows OpenSSH and Codex Desktop remote SSH; also reproducible directly from a shell.

## Reproduction
In native Termux, use the official 0.159.1 ARM64 musl binary:

```sh
# Use a fresh test directory, keeping the real Codex state untouched.
trial_dir=$(mktemp -d "$TMPDIR/codex-uds-repro.XXXXXX")
CODEX_HOME="$trial_dir" codex app-server --listen "unix://$TMPDIR/codex-uds-repro.sock"
```

Actual: immediate exit 1:

```text
Error: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The same binary accepts a JSON-RPC `initialize` request over `app-server --stdio`. The same Unix-socket test succeeds with 0.154.0. Setting `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` to the existing Termux temp directory does not fix Unix startup.

## Root cause identified in source
`codex-rs/uds/src/daemon_directory.rs`, `shared_daemon_socket_directory()` in tag `rust-v0.159.1` unconditionally executes:

```rust
let temporary_root = fs::canonicalize("/tmp")?;
```

`start_control_socket_acceptor()` calls `prepare_shared_daemon_socket_directory()` even when `--listen unix://CUSTOM_PATH` is supplied; the custom path is only a rendezvous alias. Thus a valid custom socket parent or `$TMPDIR` cannot avoid the missing `/tmp`.

A syscall trace of the isolated 0.159.1 reproducer ends its startup path with:

```text
readlinkat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp", ..., 4096) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
```

Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.1/codex-rs/uds/src/daemon_directory.rs
Transport: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.1/codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/unix_socket.rs
Introduced by the socket-isolation change: #45984 (commit 49305d74b4c0048ee44702e3dd058e08ad3b4a51).

## Expected behavior / security constraint
Either support a deterministic, platform-appropriate protected socket root on hosts without `/tmp`, or report an actionable platform-compatibility error. A supported solution must preserve the user-owned 0700 directory checks, short Unix socket paths, and the same directory exclusion in all filesystem-restricted execution backends. This is **not** a request to use arbitrary `$TMPDIR` blindly or remove the RPC socket isolation added by #45984.

## Related report / impact
#47402 concerns sandbox mount-isolation failure inside Termux + proot Debian. This report is distinct: native Termux app-server itself cannot start its Unix transport, before sandbox execution.

Rolling back to 0.154.0 restores Desktop SSH connectivity but leaves the older runtime/model catalog. Tests were run beside the existing server; no private project content or credentials are included here. Full doctor output is omitted because this standalone, unauthenticated transport reproducer isolates the failure without unrelated account/project diagnostics.
